# EvalKit

> EvalKit is a local-first kit for authoring agent evals as code. Teams write each scenario as a small TypeScript file, share agents, judges and datasets between scenarios, version them in Git, sweep configured model settings, report to CI, compare results against a base branch, and inspect or deliberately share local result files. This site is a static guide, not a hosted evaluation service.

## Documentation

- [Manual overview](https://evalkit.leostera.dev/docs/manual/): Entry point to separate Markdown chapters for setup, agents, datasets, scoring, CLI, reports, and troubleshooting. [Markdown sources](https://github.com/leostera/evalkit/tree/main/sites/evalkit.leostera.dev/src/content/docs/manual).
- [Get started](https://evalkit.leostera.dev/docs/): A walkthrough for the generated starter project. [Markdown source](https://github.com/leostera/evalkit/blob/main/sites/evalkit.leostera.dev/src/content/docs/index.md).
- [Project structure and discovery](https://evalkit.leostera.dev/docs/manual/project-structure/): `scenarios/`, directory suites, IDs, config, load errors, and explicit registries.
- [Agents under test](https://evalkit.leostera.dev/docs/manual/agents/): The adapter contract: returning turn results or streaming events.
- [Datasets](https://evalkit.leostera.dev/docs/manual/datasets/): Files and values for scenarios, computed and cached inputs, and candidate versus evaluator visibility.
- [Scorers and evals](https://evalkit.leostera.dev/docs/manual/scoring-and-evals/): Predicates, judges, metrics, `output`, `passAt`, `skip`, and checkpoint results.
- [CLI and matrices](https://evalkit.leostera.dev/docs/manual/cli-and-matrices/): Selection, sweeps, CI reporting with JUnit, `evalkit compare`, the dashboard, and sharing.
- [Results and reports](https://evalkit.leostera.dev/docs/manual/results/): Local manifests, scoring, artifacts, and running from code.
- [Troubleshooting](https://evalkit.leostera.dev/docs/manual/troubleshooting/): Common issues and current limitations.
- [API reference](https://evalkit.leostera.dev/docs/reference/api/): Every export of `@leostera/evalkit` and `@leostera/evalkit/runner`, with signatures, and where scores live on disk.
- [Migration guide from 0.5](https://github.com/leostera/evalkit/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#migrating-from-05): `evals/` to `scenarios/`, fixtures to datasets.
- [Repository](https://github.com/leostera/evalkit): Source code, contracts, tests, and examples.
- [EvalKit package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@leostera/evalkit): The repository root builds `@leostera/evalkit` with the authoring API, CLI, dashboard, and agent skills (`dist/skills/`).
- [Starter example](https://github.com/leostera/evalkit/tree/main/examples/starter): Runnable local project with default-exported scenario discovery, no registry or config.
- [Support suite example](https://github.com/leostera/evalkit/tree/main/examples/support-suite): A few dozen short scenarios in directory suites, sharing one agent, its judges, and static, computed and evaluator-only datasets.
- [Configured matrix example](https://github.com/leostera/evalkit/tree/main/examples/configured-matrix): An optional `evalkit.config.ts` and a provider-free parameter sweep.

## Implementation notes

- Start with `bunx @leostera/evalkit new ./agent-evals`, then `cd agent-evals && bun install && bun run evalkit run` to run the provider-free scenario. The CLI runs on Bun or Node 22.18+.
- The CLI discovers default-exported `scenarios/**/*.eval.ts`/`.js`; each directory directly below `scenarios/` is a suite. A file that throws on import is a load error for that file only. An optional `evalkit.config.ts` customizes discovery and execution or supplies an explicit registry.
- Authored scenarios, suites, datasets, agents, and matrices use lowercase kebab-case IDs; the CLI selects by ID. Only runs and trials have generated URIs.
- Datasets (`defineDataset`) give scenarios files and values: static (`files`, `value`, `valueFile`) or computed (`onLoad` once per process, cached; `onRun` per trial). `visibility: 'evaluator'` keeps a dataset from the agent.
- An adapter (`defineAgent`) starts a fresh session per trial; `send()` may return the reply, tool calls, and usage, or stream events with `onEvent`. Scorers get the final `output` and dataset `data`; `predicate(..., { passAt })` sets a threshold and `skip(reason)` marks a check as not applicable. Judge rules require a distinct eval-level agent. Remote Agents SDK transport and enforced timeouts are not available.
- `evalkit run --junit <file>` writes a JUnit report; `evalkit compare --base <branch> --fail-on regression` gates merge requests. Ctrl+C cancels cleanly; cancelled runs never count as failures.
- Scenario definitions are versioned in Git; reports are local files, not automatically shared. Review them for sensitive data before `evalkit build` or `evalkit share`.
- The website is static Astro served as Cloudflare Workers Static Assets. It does not run evaluations or expose an evaluation API.
